```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5, message = FALSE)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
rxode2::rxSetProgressBar(FALSE)

# Typical-value (zeroRe) and logistic models carry no omega; rxSolve warns
# about that for multi-subject event tables, which is expected here.
muffle_no_omega <- function(w) {
  if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
    invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
  }
}
solve_quiet <- function(...) {
  withCallingHandlers(rxode2::rxSolve(...), warning = muffle_no_omega)
}
```

# Source and models

```{r models, include = FALSE}
mod_adc <- readModelDb("Biesdorf_2026_cofetuzumabPelidotin")
mod_pay <- readModelDb("Biesdorf_2026_cofetuzumabPelidotin_aur0101")
mod_orr <- readModelDb("Biesdorf_2026_cofetuzumabPelidotin_orr")
mod_cbr6 <- readModelDb("Biesdorf_2026_cofetuzumabPelidotin_clinical_benefit_6mo")
mod_neut <- readModelDb("Biesdorf_2026_cofetuzumabPelidotin_neutropenia_grade3")
mod_pn <- readModelDb("Biesdorf_2026_cofetuzumabPelidotin_neuropathy_grade2")
mod_rash <- readModelDb("Biesdorf_2026_cofetuzumabPelidotin_rash_grade2")
meta_adc <- rxode2::rxode2(mod_adc)$meta
```

* Citation: `r meta_adc$reference`
* Article (open access): <https://doi.org/10.1002/cpt.70432>
* PubMed Central: <https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC13473755/>
* Supplementary Information (Data S1; Tables S1-S5 and Figures S1-S4):
  distributed with the open-access article.

Biesdorf 2026 analysed cofetuzumab pelidotin (Cofe-P, ABBV-647, PF-06647020), an
anti-PTK7 antibody-drug conjugate carrying the auristatin payload Aur0101, to
choose doses for dose optimisation in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). The
paper fits **seven** models separately, and this package carries each as its
own file:

| Model file | What it describes | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `Biesdorf_2026_cofetuzumabPelidotin` | Conjugate (ADC) popPK, two compartments | Table 1 |
| `Biesdorf_2026_cofetuzumabPelidotin_aur0101` | Unconjugated Aur0101 payload popPK, one compartment fed by deconjugation | Table 2 |
| `Biesdorf_2026_cofetuzumabPelidotin_orr` | Confirmed objective response (logistic, linear in Cavg, target-population slope) | Table S4 |
| `Biesdorf_2026_cofetuzumabPelidotin_clinical_benefit_6mo` | Clinical benefit for at least 6 months, CBR6 (logistic, linear in Cavg) | Table 3 (back-solved) |
| `Biesdorf_2026_cofetuzumabPelidotin_neutropenia_grade3` | Grade >= 3 neutropenia (logistic on log(Cavg + 1)) | Table S5 |
| `Biesdorf_2026_cofetuzumabPelidotin_neuropathy_grade2` | Grade >= 2 peripheral neuropathy (logistic on log(Cavg + 1)) | Table S5 |
| `Biesdorf_2026_cofetuzumabPelidotin_rash_grade2` | Grade >= 2 rash (logistic, linear in Cavg) | Table S5 |

All five exposure-response models are driven by the conjugate **Cavg** (ug/mL),
the individual average conjugate concentration up to the response assessment or
up to the safety event, which the source computed from post hoc estimates of the
conjugate popPK model. They have no PK layer of their own; the column `CAV` is
supplied as data.

# Population

```{r population, echo = FALSE}
pop <- rxode2::rxode2(mod_adc)$meta$population
knitr::kable(
  tibble::tibble(
    Field = c("Subjects", "Studies", "Age", "Weight", "Female (%)", "Disease", "Dosing"),
    Value = c(pop$n_subjects, pop$n_studies, pop$age_range, pop$weight_range,
              pop$sex_female_pct, pop$disease_state, pop$dose_range)
  ),
  caption = "PopPK analysis population (Biesdorf 2026 Methods and Table S3)."
)
```

The popPK analysis pooled 202 patients: 137 from the first-in-human study
B7661001 (NCT02222922; triple-negative breast, NSCLC and ovarian cancer,
0.2-3.7 mg/kg Q3W or 2.1-3.2 mg/kg Q2W) and 65 from the phase 1b NSCLC study
M19-611 (NCT04189614; 2.8 mg/kg Q3W). 161 patients (79.7%) received
2.8 mg/kg Q3W. Every dose was a 60-minute intravenous infusion. Table S3 gives
the demographics by study: weight 70.4 (18.0) and 70.1 (19.0) kg, albumin 36.3
(5.17) and 39.2 (4.61) g/L, female 84.7% and 38.5%, liver metastases 29.2% and
12.3% in B7661001 and M19-611 respectively. The exposure-efficacy set is the 60
NSCLC patients of M19-611 (28 in the target population: PTK7 expression in at
least 90% of tumour cells at 2+ intensity or more, non-squamous histology, EGFR
wild-type); the exposure-safety set is 198 patients from both studies (197 for
peripheral neuropathy).

# Check 1 -- the IIV columns of Tables 1 and 2 are variances

Both table footnotes define %CV as `SQRT[exp(omega^2) - 1] x 100`. Applying that
to the first column of every IIV row reproduces the printed %CV, so the first
column is omega^2 and enters `ini()` directly.

```{r check-iiv}
iiv <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Row,                        ~omega2, ~cv_printed,
  "Conjugate IIV on CL",        0.211,   48.4,
  "Conjugate IIV on Vc",        0.0913,  30.9,
  "Payload IIV on CL",          0.199,   47.0,
  "Payload IIV on Vc",          0.386,   68.7,
  "Payload IIV on Kdeg",        0.0210,  14.6
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(cv_from_variance = 100 * sqrt(exp(omega2) - 1),
                cv_if_sd = 100 * sqrt(exp(omega2^2) - 1))
knitr::kable(iiv, digits = 2, caption = "Printed %CV against the variance and SD readings.")
stopifnot(all(abs(iiv$cv_from_variance - iiv$cv_printed) < 0.1))
```

# Check 2 -- the residual-error rows are variances too

Tables 1 and 2 print the residual errors as bare numbers. For a residual
parameter informed by `N` observations, the relative standard error expected of a
variance is about `sqrt(2/N)` and of a standard deviation about `sqrt(1/(2N))`,
half as large. With 3391 conjugate and 3530 payload observations:

```{r check-sigma}
sig <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Row,                       ~N,   ~rse_printed,
  "Conjugate proportional",   3391, 3.20,
  "Payload proportional",     3530, 3.52,
  "Payload additive",         3530, 5.11
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(rse_if_variance = 100 * sqrt(2 / N),
                rse_if_sd = 100 * sqrt(1 / (2 * N)))
knitr::kable(sig, digits = 2, caption = "Printed %RSE of the residual terms against the two readings.")
stopifnot(all(sig$rse_printed > sig$rse_if_variance))
```

Every printed %RSE sits at or above the variance prediction and 2.7-4.3 times
the SD prediction (combined error models inflate the RSE further), so the
values are read as `$SIGMA` variances and the model files take their square
roots. The additive terms then make physical sense: `sqrt(0.0108)` = 0.104 ug/mL
for the conjugate sits at its 0.090 ug/mL LLOQ, and `sqrt(0.00276)` = 0.053 ng/mL
for the payload is about 3.5 times its 0.015 ng/mL LLOQ.

# Conjugate (ADC) pharmacokinetics

## Virtual cohort

Weights follow Table S3 by study (log-normal with the printed mean and SD). Each
arm has 200 patients.

```{r cohort}
n_sub <- 200L
rlnorm_ms <- function(n, mean, sd) {
  s2 <- log(1 + (sd / mean)^2)
  stats::rlnorm(n, log(mean) - s2 / 2, sqrt(s2))
}
set.seed(20260325)
cohort_p1b <- tibble::tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_sub),
  WT = pmin(pmax(rlnorm_ms(n_sub, 70.1, 19.0), 35), 150),
  ALB = pmin(pmax(stats::rnorm(n_sub, 39.2, 4.61), 25), 52),
  LMET = stats::rbinom(n_sub, 1, 0.123),
  STUDY_M19611 = 1L
)
```

## Simulated profiles

```{r sim-adc}
inf_dur <- 1 / 24 # 60-minute infusion, in days
tau <- 21

sim_adc_dose <- function(mgkg, cohort, seed) {
  rxode2::rxSetSeed(seed) # common random numbers across dose arms
  amt <- mgkg * cohort$WT
  dose <- data.frame(id = cohort$id, time = 0, amt = amt, rate = amt / inf_dur,
                     evid = 1L, cmt = "central")
  obs_t <- c(seq(0, 0.1, by = 0.01), seq(0.125, 2, by = 0.125), seq(2.25, 84, by = 0.25))
  obs <- data.frame(id = rep(cohort$id, each = length(obs_t)), time = rep(obs_t, times = nrow(cohort)),
                    amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
    dplyr::left_join(cohort, by = "id")
  out <- as.data.frame(solve_quiet(mod_adc, events = ev, returnType = "data.frame"))
  out$dose_mgkg <- mgkg
  out
}

doses <- c(2.1, 2.4, 2.8, 3.2)
sim_adc <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(doses, sim_adc_dose, cohort = cohort_p1b, seed = 20260325L))
```

```{r plot-adc, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Simulated conjugate concentrations after one 2.8 mg/kg dose in the phase 1b population (median and 5th-95th percentiles of the 200-patient cohort, without residual error). Compare with the 'ADC Conjugate' panel of Figure S4 of Biesdorf 2026."}
sim_adc |>
  dplyr::filter(dose_mgkg == 2.8, time <= tau, time > 0) |>
  dplyr::group_by(time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(med = median(Cc), lo = quantile(Cc, 0.05), hi = quantile(Cc, 0.95), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(time, med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1, 3, 7, 14, 21)) +
  labs(x = "Time since dose (days)", y = "Conjugate concentration (ug/mL)")
```

## Check 3 -- end-of-infusion predictions match the Figure S2 population-prediction bands

The population-prediction panel of Figure S2 (conjugate) shows dense horizontal
bands of end-of-infusion predictions, the strongest near 80 ug/mL and another
near 65 ug/mL. Because Vc scales with weight to the power 1 and the dose is per
kilogram, the typical end-of-infusion concentration depends only on the dose
and the study. At 2.8 mg/kg, the dose most patients received:

```{r check-bands}
ev_typ <- data.frame(id = c(1, 2), time = 0, amt = 2.8 * 70, rate = 2.8 * 70 / inf_dur,
                     evid = 1L, cmt = "central", WT = 70, STUDY_M19611 = c(0L, 1L)) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows(data.frame(id = c(1, 2), time = inf_dur, amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0L,
                              cmt = "central", WT = 70, STUDY_M19611 = c(0L, 1L))) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
eoi <- as.data.frame(solve_quiet(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_adc), events = ev_typ, returnType = "data.frame"))
eoi_tab <- tibble::tibble(Study = c("B7661001 (first-in-human)", "M19-611 (phase 1b)"),
                          `Typical end-of-infusion Cc (ug/mL)` = eoi$Cc,
                          `Figure S2 band (ug/mL)` = c(65, 80))
knitr::kable(eoi_tab, digits = 1)
stopifnot(all(abs(eoi$Cc / c(65, 80) - 1) < 0.05))
```

This confirms Vc and the size of the study factor on Vc (0.832 is the ratio of
the two bands). It does not say WHICH study carries the factor: swapping the
coding only swaps the two bands between the studies. Check 4 settles that.

## PKNCA analysis

```{r pknca-adc}
conc_adc <- sim_adc |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = paste0(dose_mgkg, " mg/kg Q3W")) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
conc_adc <- conc_adc |>
  dplyr::bind_rows(conc_adc |> dplyr::distinct(id, treatment) |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::arrange(treatment, id, time)
dose_adc <- tidyr::expand_grid(cohort_p1b |> dplyr::select(id, WT), dose_mgkg = doses) |>
  dplyr::transmute(id, time = 0, amt = dose_mgkg * WT, treatment = paste0(dose_mgkg, " mg/kg Q3W"))

o_conc <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_adc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
o_dose <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_adc, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
o_data <- PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  o_conc, o_dose,
  intervals = data.frame(
    start = c(0, 0), end = c(tau, 84),
    cmax = c(TRUE, FALSE), tmax = c(TRUE, FALSE), cav = c(TRUE, FALSE),
    auclast = c(FALSE, TRUE)
  )
)
nca_adc <- as.data.frame(PKNCA::pk.nca(o_data))
```

```{r pknca-adc-summary, echo = FALSE}
nca_adc |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "cav")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(median = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median) |>
  dplyr::rename("Regimen" = treatment, "Cmax (ug/mL)" = cmax, "Tmax (day)" = tmax,
                "Cavg cycle 1 (ug/mL)" = cav) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Median cycle-1 NCA parameters of the simulated phase 1b cohort.")
```

## Check 4 -- steady-state Cavg against Table 3

Table 3 lists the popPK-predicted median steady-state Cavg of the phase 1b
target population at four Q3W doses. With linear PK, the steady-state AUC over
one interval equals the single-dose AUC to infinity, so the steady-state Cavg is
the 0-84 day AUC of one dose (more than 25 half-lives of the fast phase) divided
by 21 days.

```{r check-table3-cavg}
cav_ss <- nca_adc |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast", end == 84) |>
  dplyr::mutate(cav_ss = PPORRES / tau,
                dose_mgkg = as.numeric(sub(" mg/kg Q3W", "", treatment)))
cav_tab <- cav_ss |>
  dplyr::group_by(dose_mgkg) |>
  dplyr::summarise(simulated = median(cav_ss), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::mutate(published = c(10.1, 11.6, 13.5, 15.4),
                pct_diff = 100 * (simulated / published - 1))
cav_tab |>
  dplyr::rename("Dose (mg/kg Q3W)" = dose_mgkg, "Simulated median Cavg,ss (ug/mL)" = simulated,
                "Table 3 (ug/mL)" = published, "Difference (%)" = pct_diff) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
stopifnot(
  # Structural: with the study factor on the wrong study, or a mis-transcribed
  # CL, the median moves by 20% or more.
  all(abs(cav_tab$pct_diff) < 12)
)
```

```{r nca-comparison, echo = FALSE}
knitr::kable(
  nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
    simulated = cav_ss |> dplyr::filter(dose_mgkg == 2.8) |> dplyr::transmute(cav = cav_ss),
    reference = tibble::tibble(cav = 13.5),
    label_first_column = "NCA parameter"
  ),
  caption = "Median simulated steady-state Cavg at 2.8 mg/kg Q3W against Table 3."
)
```

The simulated medians sit a few percent below Table 3 at every dose. The
direction is consistent with what the simulation cannot reproduce: the source
medians come from post hoc estimates of the actual target-population patients
(28 of them), while the simulation draws a virtual phase 1b cohort from the
Table S3 weight distribution; the reference weight used to normalise CL is not
printed (70 kg is used here); and Table 3 shows the target subgroup, whose
weight distribution is not reported. The dose ratios themselves (Cavg
proportional to dose) are reproduced exactly, as linear PK requires.

## Check 5 -- conjugate half-life against the phase 1b report

Biesdorf 2026 quotes the harmonic-mean terminal half-life of Cofe-P at
2.8 mg/kg Q3W in M19-611 as 3.01 days. That figure is an NCA estimate from the
phase 1b sampling schedule (Table S1: end of infusion + 15 minutes, day 2, day 8
and the cycle-2 pre-dose sample on day 21), which sees the distribution and
terminal phases mixed. Applying the same schedule to the simulated profiles:

```{r check-thalf}
p1b_times <- c(inf_dur + 15 / 1440, 1 + inf_dur, 7 + inf_dur, 21)
conc_sched <- sim_adc |>
  dplyr::filter(dose_mgkg == 2.8) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc)
sched <- do.call(rbind, lapply(p1b_times, function(t) {
  conc_sched |>
    dplyr::group_by(id) |>
    dplyr::slice(which.min(abs(time - t))) |>
    dplyr::ungroup()
}))
sched <- dplyr::bind_rows(sched, tibble::tibble(id = cohort_p1b$id, time = 0, Cc = 0)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time) |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = "2.8 mg/kg Q3W")
o_conc_s <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sched, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
o_dose_s <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_adc |> dplyr::filter(treatment == "2.8 mg/kg Q3W"),
                             amt ~ time | treatment + id)
nca_s <- as.data.frame(PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  o_conc_s, o_dose_s,
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 21, half.life = TRUE)
)))
thalf <- nca_s |> dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "half.life", !is.na(PPORRES)) |> dplyr::pull(PPORRES)
thalf_hm <- 1 / mean(1 / thalf)
knitr::kable(tibble::tibble(`Simulated harmonic mean t1/2 (day)` = thalf_hm,
                            `Published (day)` = 3.01), digits = 2)
# Envelope only: a three-point half-life depends on which samples the NCA
# kept, and the source's point selection is not reported.
stopifnot(abs(thalf_hm / 3.01 - 1) < 0.25)
```

The simulated harmonic mean is about 18% longer than the reported 3.01 days.
This comparator is weak: a half-life fitted to three samples across a
two-compartment profile moves by more than that depending on which samples are
used (days 1-7 alone give about 2.2 days for a typical patient, days 7-21 about
4.2 days), and the source does not say which points its NCA kept. Coding the
first-in-human study as the one carrying the study factors would shorten the
three-point half-life of a typical 70 kg patient from 3.3 to about 3.1 days,
but it would break the much stronger Table 3
check above (the median Cavg at 2.8 mg/kg would fall from 13.0 to about
10 ug/mL, 24% below the published 13.5 ug/mL), so the coding is kept.

# Unconjugated Aur0101 payload

Biesdorf 2026 describes the payload with a one-compartment model with first-order
input at the deconjugation rate Kdeg. The model was developed **separately**
from the conjugate model, so its depot is dosed directly. The paper does not
report the drug-antibody ratio, the molecular weights or the fraction of the
conjugate dose that ends up as systemically available payload, so the depot
must be dosed in Aur0101-equivalent micrograms. The structural checks below use
a unit dose; only the plot applies an illustrative conversion.

## Check 6 -- the payload half-life is the deconjugation half-life

```{r check-payload}
pay_t <- c(0, seq(0.05, 1, by = 0.05), seq(1.25, 28, by = 0.25))
ev_pay <- data.frame(id = 1, time = c(0, pay_t), amt = c(1, rep(0, length(pay_t))),
                     evid = c(1L, rep(0L, length(pay_t))), cmt = "depot",
                     WT = 70, ALB = 37, LMET = 0L, STUDY_M19611 = 0L)
pay_typ <- as.data.frame(solve_quiet(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_pay), events = ev_pay, returnType = "data.frame"))
term <- pay_typ |> dplyr::filter(time >= 7, time <= 21)
slope <- -stats::coef(stats::lm(log(Cc) ~ time, data = term))[["time"]]
knitr::kable(tibble::tibble(
  `Terminal slope, days 7-21 (1/day)` = slope,
  `Kdeg (1/day)` = 0.243,
  `t1/2 from slope (day)` = log(2) / slope,
  `Published harmonic-mean payload t1/2 (day)` = 2.95
), digits = 3)
stopifnot(abs(slope / 0.243 - 1) < 0.01, abs(log(2) / slope / 2.95 - 1) < 0.10)
```

Kdeg (0.243 /day) is about 27 times slower than CL/Vc (6.5 /day), so the payload
profile is formation-rate limited: its terminal slope is the deconjugation rate,
and the 2.85-day half-life it implies agrees with the 2.95-day harmonic-mean
payload half-life of the phase 1b study. The same slope, read off the median line
of the payload pcVPC in Figure S4 between days 7 and 21 (about 1.5 to
0.045 ng/mL), is 0.25 /day.

## Payload profile on a clinical dose (illustrative)

```{r illustrative-payload}
# NOT a model parameter and NOT a published value. Biesdorf 2026 reports no
# drug-antibody ratio, molecular weights or payload fraction. This factor was
# back-solved so that a typical 70 kg patient given 2.8 mg/kg reaches the
# day-1 payload median of about 5.9 ng/mL read off Figure S4, purely so that
# the payload model can be plotted on a clinical dose. It is kept in the
# vignette and out of the model file, and matching Figure S4 at day 1 is
# therefore not evidence for anything.
c1_per_ug <- pay_typ$Cc[which.min(abs(pay_typ$time - 1))]
payload_fraction_illustrative <- 5.9 / (c1_per_ug * 2.8 * 70 * 1000)
payload_fraction_illustrative
```

The fraction comes out near 1.9% of the conjugate mass. For orientation only,
four auristatin molecules of roughly 0.7 kDa on a 150 kDa antibody would be about
2% by mass, the right order of magnitude.

```{r sim-payload, fig.cap = "Simulated unconjugated Aur0101 after one 2.8 mg/kg dose in the phase 1b cohort, using the illustrative payload fraction (median and 5th-95th percentiles, without residual error). Compare the SHAPE with the 'Payload' panel of Figure S4; the level is calibrated, not predicted."}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20260326L)
pay_obs <- seq(0.25, 21, by = 0.25)
ev_pc <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  data.frame(id = cohort_p1b$id, time = 0, amt = payload_fraction_illustrative * 2.8 * cohort_p1b$WT * 1000,
             evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"),
  data.frame(id = rep(cohort_p1b$id, each = length(pay_obs)), time = rep(pay_obs, n_sub),
             amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "depot")
) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(cohort_p1b, by = "id")
sim_pay <- as.data.frame(solve_quiet(mod_pay, events = ev_pc, returnType = "data.frame"))
sim_pay |>
  dplyr::group_by(time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(med = median(Cc), lo = quantile(Cc, 0.05), hi = quantile(Cc, 0.95), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(time, med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1, 3, 7, 14, 21)) +
  labs(x = "Time since dose (days)", y = "Unconjugated Aur0101 (ng/mL)")
```

# Exposure-response

## Check 7 -- the logistic models reproduce Table 3

Table 3 gives, for each dose, the median steady-state Cavg of the target
population and the model-predicted probability of each endpoint at that Cavg.
Evaluating the five model files at the printed Cavg values is therefore a direct
check of the transcribed coefficients (and, for CBR6, of the back-solve).

```{r check-table3}
solve_prob <- function(model, output, cav, target = NULL) {
  ev <- data.frame(id = seq_along(cav), time = 0, amt = 0, evid = 0L, CAV = cav)
  if (!is.null(target)) ev$TARGET_POPULATION <- target
  as.data.frame(solve_quiet(model, events = ev, returnType = "data.frame"))[[output]]
}
cav_t3 <- c(10.1, 11.6, 13.5, 15.4)
t3 <- tibble::tibble(
  Endpoint = rep(c("ORR (target population)", "CBR6", "Neutropenia grade >= 3",
                   "Peripheral neuropathy grade >= 2", "Rash grade >= 2"), each = 4),
  Cavg = rep(cav_t3, 5),
  Published = c(6.52, 11.1, 20.6, 35.1,
                24.3, 34.2, 48.8, 63.6,
                16.8, 22.8, 31.0, 39.3,
                4.81, 6.85, 10.0, 13.8,
                4.78, 6.11, 8.28, 11.1),
  Model = 100 * c(solve_prob(mod_orr, "prob_orr", cav_t3, target = 1L),
                  solve_prob(mod_cbr6, "prob_clinical_benefit_6mo", cav_t3),
                  solve_prob(mod_neut, "prob_neutropenia_grade3", cav_t3),
                  solve_prob(mod_pn, "prob_peripheral_neuropathy_grade2", cav_t3),
                  solve_prob(mod_rash, "prob_rash_grade2", cav_t3))
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(Difference = Model - Published)
t3 |>
  dplyr::rename("Cavg (ug/mL)" = Cavg, "Table 3 (%)" = Published, "Model (%)" = Model,
                "Difference (percentage points)" = Difference) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Model probabilities at the Table 3 Cavg values.")
```

The CBR6, neutropenia and neuropathy models reproduce Table 3 to within 0.15
percentage points. The ORR and rash models fall a little short, and only
because their slopes are printed to two significant figures. Taking each
printed coefficient at the edge of its rounding interval brackets Table 3:

```{r check-rounding}
orr_hi <- 100 * stats::plogis(-6.555 + (0.355 + 0.035) * cav_t3)
rash_hi <- 100 * stats::plogis(-4.725 + 0.175 * cav_t3)
orr_mod <- t3$Model[t3$Endpoint == "ORR (target population)"]
rash_mod <- t3$Model[t3$Endpoint == "Rash grade >= 2"]
knitr::kable(tibble::tibble(
  Cavg = cav_t3,
  `ORR printed coefficients` = orr_mod, `ORR rounding upper edge` = orr_hi,
  `ORR Table 3` = c(6.52, 11.1, 20.6, 35.1),
  `Rash printed coefficients` = rash_mod, `Rash rounding upper edge` = rash_hi,
  `Rash Table 3` = c(4.78, 6.11, 8.28, 11.1)
), digits = 2)
stopifnot(
  # CBR6 / neutropenia / neuropathy: equal to rounding of the printed percentages.
  all(abs(t3$Difference[!t3$Endpoint %in% c("ORR (target population)", "Rash grade >= 2")]) < 0.15),
  # ORR and rash: Table 3 lies inside the band spanned by the rounding interval.
  all(c(6.52, 11.1, 20.6, 35.1) >= orr_mod - 0.01 & c(6.52, 11.1, 20.6, 35.1) <= orr_hi),
  all(c(4.78, 6.11, 8.28, 11.1) >= rash_mod - 0.01 & c(4.78, 6.11, 8.28, 11.1) <= rash_hi)
)
```

The ORR row also fixes how the target-population term enters. Table S4 lists a
"Slope Non-Target" of 0.35 and a "Slope Target" of 0.03; only the reading in
which 0.03 is an *increment* to 0.35 reproduces Table 3. Read as the target
slope itself, it would predict an ORR of 0.2% at 13.5 ug/mL instead of 20.6%.

## Replicating Figure 3

```{r plot-er, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 4.2, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 3 of Biesdorf 2026: predicted efficacy and safety probabilities against conjugate Cavg, with vertical lines at the Table 3 median steady-state Cavg for 2.1, 2.4, 2.8 and 3.2 mg/kg Q3W."}
cav_grid <- seq(5, 20, by = 0.1)
curves <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(CAV = cav_grid, p = solve_prob(mod_orr, "prob_orr", cav_grid, target = 1L),
                 Endpoint = "ORR (target population)"),
  tibble::tibble(CAV = cav_grid, p = solve_prob(mod_cbr6, "prob_clinical_benefit_6mo", cav_grid),
                 Endpoint = "CBR6"),
  tibble::tibble(CAV = cav_grid, p = solve_prob(mod_neut, "prob_neutropenia_grade3", cav_grid),
                 Endpoint = "Neutropenia grade >= 3"),
  tibble::tibble(CAV = cav_grid, p = solve_prob(mod_pn, "prob_peripheral_neuropathy_grade2", cav_grid),
                 Endpoint = "Peripheral neuropathy grade >= 2"),
  tibble::tibble(CAV = cav_grid, p = solve_prob(mod_rash, "prob_rash_grade2", cav_grid),
                 Endpoint = "Rash grade >= 2")
)
ggplot(curves, aes(CAV, 100 * p, colour = Endpoint)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = cav_t3, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  labs(x = "Cofe-P (ADC) Cavg (ug/mL)", y = "Predicted probability (%)", colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 2))
```

## Replicating Figure 1e -- target versus non-target ORR

```{r plot-orr, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 3.4, fig.cap = "Replicates the two subgroup curves of Figure 1e of Biesdorf 2026 (ORR against conjugate Cavg up to best overall response)."}
orr_curves <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(CAV = cav_grid, p = solve_prob(mod_orr, "prob_orr", cav_grid, target = 1L), Group = "Target"),
  tibble::tibble(CAV = cav_grid, p = solve_prob(mod_orr, "prob_orr", cav_grid, target = 0L), Group = "Non-target")
)
ggplot(orr_curves, aes(CAV, 100 * p, linetype = Group)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Cofe-P (ADC) Cavg (ug/mL)", y = "ORR (%)", linetype = NULL)
```

## From dose to probability with the simulated cohort

Chaining the conjugate model and the exposure-response models: the simulated
phase 1b cohort's steady-state Cavg (Check 4) is passed to the logistic models
and the probability at each dose's median Cavg is compared with Table 3. The
differences carry the few-percent Cavg shortfall of Check 4 and are shown for
information.

```{r chain, echo = FALSE}
med_cav <- cav_tab$simulated
chain <- tibble::tibble(
  `Dose (mg/kg Q3W)` = doses,
  `Median Cavg,ss (ug/mL)` = med_cav,
  `ORR (%)` = 100 * solve_prob(mod_orr, "prob_orr", med_cav, target = 1L),
  `CBR6 (%)` = 100 * solve_prob(mod_cbr6, "prob_clinical_benefit_6mo", med_cav),
  `Neutropenia >= 3 (%)` = 100 * solve_prob(mod_neut, "prob_neutropenia_grade3", med_cav),
  `Neuropathy >= 2 (%)` = 100 * solve_prob(mod_pn, "prob_peripheral_neuropathy_grade2", med_cav),
  `Rash >= 2 (%)` = 100 * solve_prob(mod_rash, "prob_rash_grade2", med_cav)
)
knitr::kable(chain, digits = 1,
             caption = "Probabilities at the simulated median steady-state Cavg (compare Table 3: ORR 6.52 / 11.1 / 20.6 / 35.1%).")
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Reference values for weight and albumin.** Biesdorf 2026 normalised
  continuous covariates to the dataset median, which it does not print.
  Table S3 gives only means (weight 70.3 kg, albumin 37.2 g/L overall), so the
  models normalise to 70 kg and 37 g/L. For the conjugate this changes the
  typical CL by `(70/ref)^0.75`; a reference of 67 or 73 kg would move typical
  exposure by about 3%.
* **Which study carries the study factor.** Tables 1 and 2 print "Study on CL"
  and "Study on Vc" without naming the reference study. For the conjugate, the
  phase 1b study M19-611 carries the factors: only that coding reproduces the
  Table 3 Cavg of the phase 1b target population (Check 4; the reverse coding
  gives about 10 instead of 13.5 ug/mL at 2.8 mg/kg). The Figure S2
  end-of-infusion bands (Check 3) confirm the Vc factor's size but not its
  direction, and the three-point half-life (Check 5) leans slightly the other
  way but is a weak comparator. The
  payload model is assumed to use the same coding for its "Study on Vc" (0.828);
  no published output tests that directly.
* **Residual errors are variances.** The residual rows of Tables 1 and 2 are
  bare numbers. They are read as NONMEM `$SIGMA` variances (Check 2) and the
  model files carry their square roots.
* **Payload dose in Aur0101 equivalents.** The payload depot must be dosed in
  Aur0101-equivalent micrograms, because the conversion from a conjugate dose
  is not reported. The illustrative fraction used above (about 1.9%) was
  back-solved from Figure S4 and is not part of the model.
* **Payload concentration scale.** The payload model returns ng/mL with a
  microgram depot. The source plots and assays the payload in ng/mL, and the
  Table 2 additive error is only plausible on that scale.
* **ORR link function.** The Results say a log link was selected for the
  efficacy endpoints, but Table S4 labels the ORR model "Linear Model", and the
  linear form reproduces Table 3 (Check 7). The table is followed.
* **ORR target-population term.** "Slope Target" (0.03) in Table S4 is encoded
  as an increment to the non-target slope (0.35), the only reading consistent
  with Table 3 and with the Results statement that the target population had a
  higher probability of response.
* **CBR6 coefficients are back-solved.** The paper prints no CBR6 coefficients.
  The intercept and slope were back-solved from the four Table 3 predictions,
  which a logit linear in Cavg fits to rounding (residual SD 0.0014 logit
  units); log(Cavg) and log(Cavg + 1) forms fit 35-40 times worse. The resulting
  curve passes through the Figure 1c fitted line (about 24% at 10 ug/mL and 80%
  at 18 ug/mL).
* **Logarithm base.** The neutropenia and neuropathy models use the natural
  logarithm of (Cavg + 1); it reproduces Table 3 to within 0.15 percentage
  points, which a base-10 logarithm would not.
* **Placeholder residual on the probability outputs.** The logistic models were
  fitted with a Bernoulli likelihood and have no residual error. A fixed
  additive SD of 0.001 is attached to each probability output only because
  rxode2 needs an observation declaration. Sample binary outcomes with
  `rbinom(n, 1, prob_*)` on the `rxSolve()` output.
* **Not extracted.** The overall-population ORR curve of Figure 1b (the model
  before the target-population covariate was added) has no printed
  coefficients and is superseded by the final ORR model. Plain clinical benefit
  rate had no significant exposure relationship and has no model. The 95%
  confidence bands of Figures 1-3 depend on the coefficient covariance matrix,
  which is not reported.
* **Exposure metric.** The exposure-response models take Cavg up to the event
  (or up to best overall response), which depends on each patient's actual
  dosing history and event time. Table 3, and the dose-to-probability chain
  above, use the steady-state Cavg instead, as Biesdorf 2026 did for its dose
  projections.
